question.text: A call option is said to be 'In the Money' (ITM) when:

answer.text: Spot price of the underlying is higher than the strike price
Spot price of the underlying is lower than the strike price
Spot price of the underlying equals the strike price

explanation.text: The Logic: A call is ITM when the spot price of the underlying is higher than the strike price, because the holder can buy at the lower strike and immediately realise a gain at the higher spot. A put is ITM in the opposite case, when the spot price is lower than the strike. When spot equals strike the option is at-the-money (ATM); when the relationship is reversed it is out-of-the-money (OTM). The Trap: Saying spot is lower than strike describes a put ITM, not a call ITM. Spot equal to strike is ATM. A positive premium is true of every live option and does not indicate moneyness. Note: Rewrote both the options and the explanation in plain English (e.g., 'higher than', 'lower than') to avoid raw '<'/'>' characters that previously truncated the explanation when parsed as XML.
